Join one of Europe's fastest-growing companies. 1 UI/UX Designer (m/f/d) Your role

You own how fonio feels on the web. Our website is our most important storefront - and right now it's not where it needs to be. You don't build one nice page, you build a system: a design system and landing page templates that roll out into localized pages across 9+ markets. Continuous optimization, not a one-off redesign. You design and ship - you own the build end-to-end, not a handoff to engineering. We're building an AI operating system for SMBs - people should feel that on the website.

What to expect

 * You own the design and continuous optimization of our website and landing pages

 * You build a scalable design system with reusable components

 * You develop landing page templates that localize across all markets (DACH, FR, IT, ES, UK, PL, US, and more)

 * You design and ship live yourself - full ownership from concept to published page

 * You think in user journey, conversion, and responsive design

 * You work closely with the Creative Director on brand direction

Who we're looking for

 * Several years of experience as a UI/UX or web designer focused on converting websites (portfolio required)

 * You think in systems and components, not individual pages

 * You build and ship yourself

 * Experience with design systems and localization across multiple markets

 * You understand conversion and think in journeys

 * German + good English

What we offer

 * Competitive salary: €65,000-€90,000

 * Equity - you're building this, so you should own a piece of it.

 * Food & drinks - lunch and dinner are on us at the Vienna office (plus all the drinks you want, and yes, we have protein bars and vitamins too).

 * Relocation bonus (if you still need to move to Vienna)

 * Equipment of your choice - whatever makes you happy.

 * Regular team offsites.

Hiring process

 * 15 min intro call

 * 30 min skill interview

 * 20 min culture fit with the founders

OPTIMUSE is a Vienna-based AI startup revolutionizing the real estate and construction industry. We br... 1 Software Engineer - Engine Integration (m/f/d) Job description
Our Product Engineers are domain experts first, developers second. They build Engines - the simulations and models that capture how buildings actually behave - fast, and increasingly with AI. But these prototypes live on GitHub and only run on laptops: untested against the platform, unavailable to customers.

That's the gap you close. You're the key counterpart to our Product Engineers: you understand what an Engine computes, how, and why - well enough to decide where each piece belongs, hand off what belongs to other teams, and build the rest yourself. No finished spec lands in your inbox. You read other people's code, ask the right questions, and turn a working prototype into a service we can run and trust. We work in a strongly agentic way - so will you.

Your mission
 * Run our Engines and make them better - correct, fast, observable. When results look wrong, you can tell whether it's the data, the integration, or the physics.

 * Onboard new prototypes - understand the method and edge cases; judge what's production-ready and what needs a rewrite.

 * Find the right home for each function - decompose monoliths and define the interfaces and data contracts that make those boundaries real.

 * Integrate - with Planning and our Systems Architects, translating between domain and platform language, then build what remains yourself.

 * Make the next Engine easier than the last - shape the conventions that let prototypes arrive closer to integration-ready.

You won't do this alone: DevOps, App/Experience, AI, and Data & Flows already own their domains.

Your profile
 * Several years of professional software engineering across the stack, centre of gravity in the backend.

 * Python and TypeScript - strong in one, comfortable in the other, attached to neither.

 * The ability to read and judge code you didn't write, including scientific and numerical code.

 * A low-ego, collaborative style with domain experts, and the skill to explain trade-offs to people who think in physics, not architecture.

 * Professional English. German is a plus, not a requirement.

Nice-to-have

 * Geometry in code (computational geometry, meshes, CAD or BIM/IFC).

 * Simulation and numerical methods (thermal/energy simulation, FEM/CFD, solvers).

 * Real experience with AI and agentic workflows.

 * Productionizing research or prototype code (ML pipelines, scientific computing, quant models).

 * Building-industry or energy-domain exposure.

Why us?
 * Real impact. The Engines you integrate don't sit in a demo - they feed real investment decisions and move the platform forward in tangible ways.

 * The full solution chain. From digital twin to performance monitoring - you work across a complete product portfolio, not isolated one-off projects. Every Engine you bring in has a real place in the whole.

 * Flexible working models. Home-office option and a modern office in the heart of Vienna.

 * And the day-to-day works too. Daily meal allowance (€5/day), regular team events, free snacks.

 * Compensation: €60,000 - €75,000 gross/year, depending on your experience.

About us
OPTIMUSE is a Vienna-based AI startup revolutionizing the real estate and construction industry. We bring insights to the world's largest asset class that it never had before - both for new developments and existing portfolios. Our AI Hans delivers instant, deep engineering insight into costs, risks and optimization potential, grounded in building physics, simulation and engineering. Backed by international investors and a team of ~25 people from around 10 nations. Become a part of it!

1 Postdoctoral Researcher (Quantitative Methods) (m/f/d) Advertisement No. SB26-0125.

Full-time position (40 hours/week), initially limited to two years.

In this position you will

 * Survey leadership
 ** Design and implement online surveys and embedded survey experiments (e.g. vignette and conjoint experiments) in LimeSurvey.
 ** Lead questionnaire development in close consultation with the Principal Investigator (PI).
 ** Coordinate survey implementation across Tunisia, Egypt, and Morocco, including social media-based participant recruitment.
 ** Lead the analysis of survey and experimental data using advanced quantitative methods.
 * Data collection
 ** Oversee the implementation of face-to-face survey in cooperation with a survey company in Morocco.
 ** Ensure high standards of data quality, research ethics compliance and data management throughout the data collection process.
 ** Contribute to and co-manage the coding of de facto (forced) migration policy data.
 * Research
 ** Develop and submit at least two articles to leading international peer-reviewed journals based on the survey data, in co-authorship with the PI.
 ** Contribute to theoretical development within the project and to further publications arising from MixedRivals.
 * Collaboration
 ** Present project findings at international conferences, workshops and other academic events.
 ** Contribute actively to project meetings, workshops, project documentation and grant reporting.
 ** Collaborate closely with an interdisciplinary and international research team.

Your profile

For your application, we require evidence of the following qualifications:

 * Completed PhD in political science, conflict studies, social psychology, or a related social science discipline, preferably with distinction (the PhD degree must be awarded at the latest by 15th of December 2026).
 * Advanced expertise in quantitative methods, including inferential statistics and causal inference.
 * Demonstrated experience in the design, implementation and analysis of online surveys and survey experiments, combined with advanced quantitative skills in R and/or Stata.
 * A strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals, appropriate to career stage, together with excellent analytical and academic writing skills.
 * Excellent command of English (minimum C1), both written and spoken.
 * Strong organizational, interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively in an international research team.
 * Willingness to relocate to Austria and work regularly on site at Campus Krems.

In addition, the following criteria are desirable:
 * Previous research on inter-group perceptions, inequalities, (forced) migration and/or violence
 * Knowledge of or experience in North Africa, particularly Morocco
 * Knowledge of de facto migration policies in Africa
 * Experience with LimeSurvey or comparable survey software.
 * Knowledge of qualitative research methods (e.g. interviews) and/or qualitative analysis software such as MAXQDA
 * Programming skills (e.g. Python)
 * Knowledge of French and/or Arabic
 * Previous experience working in international collaborative research projects

We look forward to receiving your compelling online application by 7 October 2026.

The following documents must be submitted:

 * Curriculum Vitae, including publication list and contact details for two or three references
 * Motivation letter clearly explaining how you could contribute to the project tasks and how the position fits with your previous and future research agenda
 * Two writing samples, preferably first-authored peer-reviewed publications or single-authored academic work 
 * A brief description of your previous survey research experience, including the surveys and/or datasets you have worked with and your role in their design, implementation and/or analysis
 * Copies of degrees and transcripts
